title: The home as sangat
hookLine: a household can be a small congregation
tomorrow: now Simran's own family tries it at bedtime. who falls asleep?

cards: The evening noise in Aman's parents' house is the TV news, loud, so his dad can hear it from the kitchen.
On Sunday, Simran and Bebe come over with a box of sweets, and the living room fills up: three generations, two families a week joined, one couple still a little careful with each other.
Then, at sunset, Aman's dad reaches for the remote. He doesn't change the channel. He turns it off, and asks Bebe if she'd lead Rehras.

teach.b: Rehras Sahib is the evening bani, a set of hymns read or recited around sunset. And this is where the word sangat earns its keep.

A sangat is a congregation, and it's easy to picture it only at the gurdwara, rows of people on the floor before the Guru Granth Sahib. But on ang 72, Guru Nanak asks a plain question and gives a plain answer.
In paraphrase: how is the true sangat known?

teach.h: ANG 72: WHERE THE NAME IS SPOKEN.
teach.b: It's where the Name of the One is spoken. The test isn't the building, the size or the dome.

teach.h: THE TEST IS WHAT'S SAID, NOT WHERE.
teach.b: It's what's said in the room. So a household can be a small sangat.

A living room with the TV off, a gutka passed from hand to hand, a grandmother leading and a father-in-law who mispronounces half the words and keeps going anyway. Here's what this offers a tense house this week.
A fight, a job hunt and a new marriage don't get solved in one evening.
But for the length of Rehras, everyone in the room faces the same direction. Nobody has to find the right words for each other.
The words are already there. Halfway through, Simran sees Aman's hand find Jasleen's on the couch. Nobody mentions it.

how: Some Sikh families read or listen to Rehras Sahib together at sunset and Kirtan Sohila before sleep, sometimes from a gutka passed around the room, making the home a small sangat.

games.q: what does “the home as sangat” mean?
o: a gurdwara built inside a family's house
a family that only prays at the gurdwara together
a household that becomes a small congregation

games.q: a living room, a sangat — tap the pairs.
p: where the Name of the One is spoken
a small prayer book of banis

s: a sangat only exists inside a gurdwara
on ang 72, the true sangat is known where the Name of the One is spoken.
Rehras Sahib is the evening bani, read around sunset
a family can read or recite it together at home.
a home sangat needs someone who pronounces every word perfectly
Aman's dad mispronounced half the words and kept going anyway.

games.q: your house is tense after a family argument, and someone suggests evening prayers together. another says, 'we're not in the mood; let's wait until things are fine.' what does today's lesson say?
o: gather anyway; for a while, everyone faces the same direction.
wait until everyone has made up, so the prayer is sincere.
pray separately, each in their own room, to avoid trouble.
games.why: the evening didn't fix the fight. but during Rehras nobody had to find words for each other; the words were already there.

practice: Think of one person you'd like to sit with in quiet for a few minutes, near you or far away. If you can, send them a short text now, something like, thinking of you this evening.
Then put the phone face down and sit as if they were in the room with you.

wordCard.voice: The home as sangat. A household that becomes a small congregation whenever the Name is spoken in it.

orig.note: Gurmukhi: sangat, a congregation; ang 72 knows it by the Name spoken there.

carryVoice: A small sangat: a room becomes one the moment the Name is spoken in it, TV off. See you tomorrow.

sources.ref: Ang 72 (Sri Raag, Guru Nanak: satsangat kaisee jaaneeai, jithai eko naam vakhaaneeai), paraphrased
